meta.notes: Each question supports two views. The default view explains why the key is correct: 'takeaway' is the clinical rule and each option carries its own rationale. questions.stem: A nurse notices that four patients in the past two weeks received scheduled morning insulin more than an hour late. She has reported each delay to the charge nurse, and each time was told the unit was short-staffed. Which action best demonstrates a Standard of Professional Performance?

options.text: Continue reporting each late dose to the charge nurse as it occurs
options.rationale: She has already done this four times with the same result. Repeating an action that has not worked leaves the situation exactly where it started.

options.text: Bring the pattern of late doses to the unit practice council with a proposed change
options.rationale: Four late doses in two weeks is a pattern, and patterns are system problems. Quality of practice and leadership are both Professional Performance standards.

options.text: Stay after her shift to give the insulin herself when the unit is short
options.rationale: Self-sacrificing and it conceals the problem. If she absorbs the gap personally the data disappears and the unit never fixes it.

options.text: Ask the provider to change the insulin to a later administration time
options.rationale: Unsafe. Insulin timing follows meals and glucose, not staffing, and this hands a nursing workflow problem to a provider.

questions.takeaway: An individual incident goes to the charge nurse. A pattern goes to the practice council, the policy, or QI.
questions.strategy: When a stem says already or each time, that option is disqualified. When two options sit in the same category, the tiebreaker is effectiveness, not correctness.

steps.detail: Polarity is positive. Key word: best. More than one option may be true, so you are ranking them.
She has already done this four times with the same result.
Self-sacrificing and it conceals the problem.
Unsafe.

elimination.verdict: That leaves B. Four late doses in two weeks is a pattern, and patterns are system problems.
